records.c: Install the game vectors and reset the SID driver. Set up the load's five table pointers in $F2-$FB, initialise the video, title and object state, then enter the main round loop.
Call the second round's setup, reset scrolling and sprite state and redraw the map before continuing in the main loop.
Refresh the HUD life pointers and choose the round's tune through the two-entry table at $291D.
Latch CIA1 port A and run player and object updates. A pending map refresh selects the redraw pipeline before the active stage tick. The keyboard pause is polled separately at $2882.
Advance the stage counter, update spawns, process the weapon button and time and use the scroll and sprite pipelines before checking the completion and death flags.
Request an effect, delay, then increment the round index. Enter the next round when the index is 1 and call the disk loader when it reaches 2.
Align the restart column to a 64-column boundary and reset transient sprite state. Spend an attempt, or take the game-over path when the attempt counter underflows.
Show game over, update the high-score table and spend a continuation, then poll fire before deciding whether to restart or resume.
Display the level-cleared banner with the glyph for 2 and transfer control to $BA03, which loads disk file B.
The two tune IDs requested by the load A round loop, indexed by the local round counter.
Read a little-endian pointer from the two-entry table at $2931 using the round index and jump through $14.
Addresses of the initial setup routines for rounds 1 and 2.
High byte of the first round setup pointer.
Clear the scroll row and timer fields and select the 512-byte row stride at $277E.
Show the round-one-clear banner and prepare the initial map row and timer fields for the second round.
Jump through the two-entry table at $299D according to the current round.
Pointers to the round-specific palette and initial object setup wrappers.
High byte of the first round palette handler pointer.
Set the first round's three playfield colours and pass the table at $39FF to $39D4.
Set the second round's three playfield colours and pass the table at $3A25 to $39D4.
Draw the high scores, title, fire prompt and copyright and music credits. Choose tune 8 and wait for fire on CIA1 port A.
Twelve custom glyph codes spelling NINJA SPIRIT.
Nineteen glyph codes spelling PRESS FIRE TO START.
First 38-glyph credit line copied into the title screen.
Second 38-glyph title credit line.
Third 38-glyph title credit line, including the C64 programming credit.
Twenty-two glyph codes for the Martin Walker music credit.
Reset four weapon-related HUD entries and clear the adjacent selector state.
Set the starting viewport and sprite slots and place two figures. Move the player down to Y=$91 with shape $AF, then deactivate the two foreground slots.
Recognise the Space matrix value $EF and latch the press until release. Clear the weapon state array, cycle the selection in $25D2 through 0, 2, 4 and 6 and request a HUD update.
Scan the round's placement records and compare their columns and rows with the camera window. Call $32B9 with the record's pointer while it is in range and clear its per-entry marker when it leaves.
Low bytes of the map columns compared with the current viewport column.
High bytes of those columns, compared with the active map page before checking X and Y.
Map row for each placement. The scanner tests it against the current row and its lower margin.
Work flags for each placement. The scanner clears the corresponding byte when its placement leaves the active viewport.
Map placement callbacks for this load. The scanner at $2BCE selects one of 51 pointers and jumps to it via $14.
High bytes of the interleaved placement-handler pointers are read at $2C14.
Lock the camera at the current column and count 80 placement ticks before allocating four component slots. Initialise the large enemy and start its tune once the slots are available.
Four object types assigned to the component slots in the round-two encounter.
Initial sprite pointers paired with the four component types.
Advance the placement counter toward $14 and choose the encounter entry or active path according to its value.
Temporarily set boss-area camera coordinates, redraw the map and write the bottom strip. Restore the previous camera values before returning.
At every eighth tick, advance the defeat delay and choose a burst origin from the indexed coordinates. At count $28, increment the round-complete state.
Request a four-part effect, recolour the four allocated slots and set the leading slot’s type.
Every 64 ticks, try to allocate a sprite and place it at one of four indexed screen positions.
Four X coordinates used by the entrance spawn at $2F32.
Four Y coordinates paired with the entrance-effect horizontal positions.
Eight horizontal step bytes indexed by the entrance spawning phase.
Eight vertical step bytes paired with the horizontal entrance velocities.
Sprite pointer table indexed by the entrance effect’s local phase.
Eight preset horizontal origins for the defeat burst routine.
Vertical partners to the eight defeat-burst X positions.
Require a clear placement flag, the right stage-tick phase and a free slot. Use the placement coordinates and start the actor at shape $77 with type $0D.
At 128-tick intervals initialise a free slot at fixed X and Y, using type $15.
At 32-tick intervals choose one of four starts using the random state and initialise its shape and horizontal motion.
Four possible initial horizontal positions for the randomly placed object.
Horizontal velocity selected with the object’s starting lane.
Vertical velocity selected with the initial lane.
Initial sprite pointer for each of the four random lanes.
Perform a one-in-64 random test, then try a free slot and start a type-$0C actor at the placement coordinates.
Find a free slot, position it from the map placement and initialise a type-$0C actor with upward velocity $FB.
Call the type-9 spawn helper and count successful placements. Select the alternate state every eighth successful allocation.
Test the placement flag and the 64-tick phase, then reserve a free slot. Initialise it using the placement coordinates, shape $67, colour $0C and type 9.
Call the shared spawn helper and change the successful result’s type to $0E.
Shift the 128-tick spawn phase and reserve a slot at the placement row. Initialise the type-$10 object with its hit and animation fields clear.
Wait for the 128-tick phase and a free slot. Use the mapped placement row, initialise a type-5 actor and advance the shared spawn counter.
Convert the placement’s map column to the horizontal coordinate relative to the camera before setting its row.
Subtract the map origin row and convert to pixels. Add the visible screen top and fine scroll before storing the sprite Y.
The attribute byte returned by the shared map query at $127B for the tile read from the stage map.
Scan active logical slots and select each slot’s type handler. Subtract the camera movement from object coordinates and check the new position against the viewport limits before dispatch.
Tail-jump through the temporary object handler pointer at $14.
26 little-endian pointer entries indexed by twice the active slot type at $8E,X. The update pass at $3267 skips a zero type before fetching its pointer.
High bytes of the interleaved object-handler pointers are read at $3278.
Left-side extent used by the collision rectangle code at $1740.
Per-type flag gating the collision callback in the shared pass at $1586.
Top-side extent read by $1740 when constructing an object’s tile rectangle.
Bottom-side extent read by $1740 to bound the vertical overlap test.
If its hit count is $FF, emit intermittent random bursts and set completion after the defeat delay. Otherwise test player overlap and process hit colour, cooldown and health for its component group.
Fold the animation phase into a three-bit index and choose four consecutive enemy shapes for the four component slots.
Horizontal phase data preceding the type-$15 handler.
Vertical phase data used with the same encounter motion phase.
Parallel values for the motion routine’s phase transitions.
Check player overlap, toggle between two shape pointers and process the actor’s pending hit and cooldown.
Advance the slot delay, sample the map above the sprite and choose the movement or hit response based on the map and its hit flag.
Test contact with the player and integrate the object’s velocities on alternate ticks.
Test contact and integrate two velocity steps every fourth tick. When hit, select type $0B and initial effect pointer $AA.
Test player overlap and transform a hit actor into an effect. Request sound $0E and award one BCD score unit.
Advance the pickup animation and try to allocate a spark every fourth raster tick. Randomise the spark’s offsets around the parent object.
If the attack hit byte is set, award one score unit and replace the object with the shared effect.
Three horizontal offsets applied to the newly allocated child’s horizontal motion.
Three vertical velocities for the spawned child sprites.
Initial shape pointers selected for the three child sprites.
The actor’s animation reads these shapes by its current phase.
Mark its map placement as active and move up one screen pixel per pass until reaching Y=$A8.
Keep its placement marked active and advance its initial animation once every eighth count until the shape reaches $6A.
Eight shape values used during the actor’s early stage.
Nine horizontal velocities selected by the player’s relative position.
Nine corresponding vertical velocities.
Shape pointer paired with each direction slot.
Copy the parent X and Y to the child and clear its hit flag. Set its type and colour to $0A.
Restore the background colour, process the boss hit cooldown and increase its hit tally. The comparison with 30 selects the defeat path.
Test player contact, process the local hit flash and trigger sound $0B when the actor takes a hit.
Check the map under the object. Process a pending hit according to its colour variant, awarding one score unit on the ordinary path.
On a pending hit, add one score unit and choose a special response for colour 7 or the shared hit effect otherwise.
Fill each of the 19 playfield rows in colour RAM from a single colour byte selected by the row.
First set of 19 row colour values consumed by the playfield colour writer.
Nineteen more colour-$0C bytes following the nineteen row values drawn by $39D4.
Nineteen row colour values for the second round.
Low three bits select the current group of four component shapes.
